Definition: from G473 and G5547; an opponent of the Messiah:--antichrist.
BiblicalUsage: Antichrist is the opponent of the Messiah, and John is the only writer who names him. He writes that many antichrists have already come, that the spirit of antichrist denies that Jesus is the Christ, and that the one who denies the Father and the Son is the antichrist.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe John wrote about antichrist so that we would not be fooled: the test is not signs or wonders but the confession of Jesus Christ come in the flesh. Many antichrists have already come, and I hold that the spirit that denies the Son is the same spirit in every age, and it is to be resisted, not debated.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
